title: Generation of image data with low signal- and contrast-to-noise ratio for the development of image processing methods in contrast-enhanced MRI
summary:
In medical imaging using MRI, it is very often necessary to administer a contrast agent. For example, this is what makes tumours visible to the radiologist in the MRI image in the first place or allows them to be better characterized. The larger the amount of contrast medium, the more clearly the radiologist can see the accumulation. In the image, the contrast medium then has a lot of signal compared to the surroundings. The contrast medium is therefore very important for the examination. Sometimes, however, it would be desirable if the radiologist could see the contrast medium even more clearly - for example, if the image quality is not so good.

We have therefore developed an algorithm in our clinic that can calculate improved images with good signal from images with poor signal. So far, however, we have only been able to test this algorithm on artificial images, i.e., in which the signal of the contrast agent has been artificially lowered compared to the surroundings. In the next step, we would like to test the algorithm on real MRI images that have a rather poor signal - in other words, on which the radiologist cannot see the enhancement of the contrast agent as well as usual. We achieve this by taking images with a lower amount of contrast agent than usual. We then pass these images to our algorithm. In the end, we want to compare the result, i.e. the improved images, with the standard examination in terms of image quality.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Participants gave written informed consent to participate in the study based on thourough oral and written information.
-Participants are legally capable and mentally able to follow the instructions of the study personnel.
Exclusion criteria:
-If the patients are pregnant or breastfeeding. A missing period in women of childbearing age, which could indicate a possible pregnancy, is considered an exclusion criterion. A pregnancy test will not be carried out. However, there is no health risk to the participant or her child assumed as a result of participating in the study.
-If the participant is under guardianship or has been placed in an institution by order of the authorities or court.
-If the participant suffers from claustrophobia ("claustrophobia").
-If there is foreign material in/on the body that is unsuitable for MRI.
-If lying down for long periods constitutes a burden for the participant, for example due to a back problem.
